specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) spatial search on a 2D graphene (honeycomb) lattice, using the Dirac point in the spectrum, with a modified site-marking scheme. The abstract gives no explicit equations, so only the standard CTQW search framework is reconstructed.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One small instance: a CTQW search with Hamiltonian H = -gamma*A + oracle term on a tiny honeycomb lattice (periodic, e.g. 2x2 unit cells = 8 sites), with a single marked site. The paper's specific marking modification, the Dirac-point tuning of parameters, multi-marking variants and the amplitude-transfer protocol are outside the scope and not reconstructed.

symbols.domain: positive integer, N=8 in the tiny instance (assumed)

symbols.meaning: adjacency matrix of the honeycomb lattice graph
symbols.domain: N x N real symmetric 0/1 matrix

symbols.meaning: strength of the marking term on site w (the abstract's modified marking scheme is unspecified)

equations.label: Schrodinger evolution
equations.description: Continuous-time quantum walk evolution under a time-independent Hamiltonian (hbar=1).
equations.justification: Standard definition of a CTQW; the abstract only mentions continuous-time quantum walk search.

equations.label: Lattice hopping Hamiltonian
equations.description: Walk Hamiltonian on the graphene lattice via the adjacency matrix; its spectrum has a Dirac point for the infinite lattice.
equations.justification: Common CTQW convention; the abstract mentions the graphene lattice and the Dirac point but gives no Hamiltonian.
assumptions: Periodic boundary conditions in the tiny instance

equations.label: Marked-site search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard oracle-type marking by an on-site potential. The abstract says the paper changes the standard marking method, so this is only a generic placeholder.
equations.justification: Generic Chen-style marking chosen as the simplest construction; it is not the paper's modified marking.
assumptions: Value of epsilon is not given and is to be tuned numerically

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Uniform superposition over lattice sites as the starting state.
equations.justification: Standard choice in spatial search; the paper's initial state is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Uniform start rather than a Dirac-point eigenstate

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of finding the walker at the marked site at time t; search succeeds if it is large at some t*.
equations.justification: Standard figure of merit for spatial search.

registers.name: site
registers.size: ceil(log2 N) = 3 qubits for N=8 (or N-dimensional single-particle space)
registers.role: walker position on lattice sites, with sites indexed by integers 0..N-1 in computational-basis encoding

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over all lattice sites (assumed).

steps.description: Build the adjacency matrix A of the small periodic honeycomb lattice and set H_0 = -gamma A.
Add a marking term at site w to form H.
Evolve under H for time t, scanning epsilon, gamma and t.
Compute P_w(t) and select the time t* that maximizes it.

specification.measurement: Measure the site register in the computational basis at time t*; success means obtaining w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Scan epsilon and t to locate the maximum of P_w(t); no other postprocessing is justified.
assumptions: Tiny instance: honeycomb lattice with 8 sites, periodic boundaries, one marked site
Generic on-site marking is used in place of the paper's modified marking
missing_information: Exact modified marking scheme used in the paper
Parameter values (gamma, epsilon) tuned to the Dirac point
Scaling of search time and success probability
